title: Hospital Account (Encounter Billing) Payment Application and Statement Consolidation Terms
content:
All patient-due Hospital Account (Encounter Billing) accounts of one patient are serviced together.

## Terms

1. A payment the patient designates to a specific account is applied to that account only.
2. An undesignated payment is applied across the patient's patient-due accounts in the payment-application order of the patient class schedule, each account receiving at most its current patient balance before the next account is reached.
3. Where the patient class terms provide that credit balances offset open balances, a credit balance on one account is applied to the patient's other patient-due accounts in the same order before any refund is considered, and only the credit left after that offset is refundable.
4. Summary statements consolidate every patient-due account of the patient into one mailing per statement cycle, as the statement-consolidation term provides, but each account carries its own statement sequence and its own first statement date.
5. A card payment larger than the card payment maximum is refused and must be split or paid by ACH bank draft.

## Worked illustration (hypothetical balances)

A patient has two patient-due accounts: account A with the older service start date and a balance of 200.00, and account B with a balance of 400.00. Under an oldest-service-start-date-first order, an undesignated payment of 300.00 brings account A to 0.00 with 200.00 and applies the remaining 100.00 to account B, leaving 300.00 there. The same payment designated to account B is applied to account B only, leaving account A at 200.00.

## Points of reading

- Consolidation joins the mailing, not the accounts: the first statement date of each account stays its own.
- A designation by the patient decides the account; the payment-application order governs only an undesignated payment.
